samples.summary: New slide-inline guard accepts an inline with no `style`; every downstream reader dereferences `inline.style` unconditionally, so such a stored inline crashes canvas layout and PPTX export for every viewer
samples.evidence: The new `assertValidSlideInlines` only rejects a *non-object* `style` (`inline.style !== undefined && inline.style !== null && typeof !== 'object'`), so `{ text: 'x' }` with no style passes. Consumers that the diff does not show: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:777` reads `inline.style.image` unconditionally inside `measureSegments` (TypeError on undefined), and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:291` (`rPrXml`) reads `s.bold` on the same value straight off `runToXml` (`text.ts:226`). The docs arm of the very same controller requires a present object style (`docs-content.controller.ts:437`), so a payload rejected through `blocks[*]` is accepted through a deck's text bodies/notes/layout placeholders and then breaks readers rather than the caller. Fix belongs on the new guard (require an object `style`, or make readers default it).

samples.summary: The guard tolerates a slide block with `inlines` entirely absent, but the shared docs layout engine dereferences `block.inlines` unconditionally — the same crash class the guard was added to close is still reachable by simply omitting the field
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideInlines` returns early for `undefined`/`null` (documented as legitimate for placeholder bodies), and `assertValidSlideBlocks` never requires the field. Out-of-diff consumers: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:152/154` (`resolveBlockInlines` returns `block.inlines` / calls `block.inlines.map`) and `measureSegments` at `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:767` iterates `inlines.length` — undefined propagates to a TypeError. Nothing normalizes slide blocks on read: `packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts` has no `blocks`/`inlines` handling, and `writeSlidesRoot` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93`) stores the JSON verbatim. Backend spec line 1008 ('accepts a slide text block that omits id/inlines') shows the tolerance is deliberate, so the fix is either defaulting `inlines` to `[]` at the writer/reader or rejecting the omission.

finding.summary: PPTX theme `<a:srgbClr val>` sink bypasses the new `toRgbHexColor` normalizer the diff establishes for every other color sink
finding.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84` still does `const hex = escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]))` → `<a:srgbClr val="${hex}"/>`, where `toSrgbHex` (theme.ts:64) is only `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`. The diff's new invariant (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:52-60: "every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number") does not hold for this file because it never routes through `colorChildXml`. `themes[]` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and the new `assertValidSlidesBody` validates only that `themes` is an array (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:472-478), so an API caller can put `rgb(255,0,0)`, `''`, or `a"/><x y="` in `theme.colors[role]` and the exported deck carries a schema-invalid (escaped-but-non-hex) `ST_HexColorRGB` that PowerPoint refuses to open.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes theme.ts as emitting `escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(...))` with `toSrgbHex` being a bare `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`. The actual file is the opposite: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:76-78 defines `toSrgbHex` as `return toRgbHexColor(hex) ?? '000000';`, importing `toRgbHexColor` from `@wafflebase/docs` at theme.ts:1 — the same normalizer color.ts:1/59 uses, with the same '000000' backstop. The emit site at theme.ts:97-98 passes that normalized value straight into `<a:srgbClr val="${hex}"/>` with no escaping needed. packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:113-143 shows `toRgbHexColor` returns only `/^[0-9A-F]{6}$/` or `undefined` (non-string -> undefined, unparseable -> undefined), so the adversarial values the finding names (`rgb(255,0,0)`, `''`, `a"/><x y="`) become `FF0000`, `000000`, `000000` — never a schema-invalid ST_HexColorRGB and never an attribute break. A repo-wide grep for `<a:srgbClr val=` under packages/slides/src returns only color.ts:60 (normalized), theme.ts:98 (normalized), and image.ts:54-55 (hardcoded literals), so the claimed invariant violation does not exist anywhere in the export path. The described code is not present.

finding.summary: Sibling object-literal attribute lookups (`DASH_VAL`, `KIND_TO_OOXML`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML`, `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE`) were left as prototype-chain-walking `Record` lookups after the diff converted ALGN/UNDERLINE/PRST/DOCX_ALIGNMENTS to Maps for exactly that reason
finding.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:122/143 `DASH_VAL[stroke.dash] ?? 'dash'` → `<a:prstDash val="…"/>`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:55-56 `KIND_TO_OOXML[a.kind] ?? 'triangle'` / `SIZE_TO_OOXML[a.size] ?? 'med'`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/layout.ts:53 `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE[layout.id] ?? 'blank'`. All four read persisted, PUT-settable values (`stroke.dash`, arrowhead kind/size, `layouts[].id` — none validated by the new `assertValidLayout`), so a stored `'constructor'`/`'toString'` resolves to an inherited `Object.prototype` member, survives the `??` fallback and is stringified into an OOXML attribute — the precise failure mode the diff documents at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:62-69 and packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:110-118.

verdict.reason:
The finding is a presence claim that four sibling lookups were "left as prototype-chain-walking Record lookups", but all four are already Maps consumed via Map.get in the working tree, and the quoted bracket-index expressions do not exist anywhere in the repo.

Verified directly:
- shape.ts:132 defines `const DASH_VAL = new Map<string, string>([['dashed','dash'],['dotted','sysDot']])`, consumed at shape.ts:153 as `DASH_VAL.get(stroke.dash) ?? 'dash'`. The claimed `DASH_VAL[stroke.dash] ?? 'dash'` at lines 122/143 is absent; lines 122-130 are a doc comment stating it is a Map "not an object literal" for exactly the prototype-chain reason the finding raises.
- connector.ts:45 and connector.ts:64 define KIND_TO_OOXML and SIZE_TO_OOXML as `new Map<string, string>`, consumed at connector.ts:72-73 as `KIND_TO_OOXML.get(a.kind) ?? 'triangle'` and `SIZE_TO_OOXML.get(a.size) ?? 'med'` — not the claimed `[a.kind]` / `[a.size]` at lines 55-56.
- layout.ts:31 defines BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE as `new Map<string, string>`, consumed at layout.ts:60 as `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE.get(layout.id) ?? 'blank'` — not the claimed `[layout.id]` at line 53.

A repo-wide Grep for the four symbol names returns only these Map definitions and their .get call sites (the only other hits are stale .agent-review/ JSON artifacts from a prior review stage, not source). A scan of packages/slides/src/export/pptx for `Record<` and `] ??` finds no bracket-indexed fallback lookup for any of the four symbols; the remaining Record<> tables (color.ts:4, animation.ts:53/72/111/121/139/149) are keyed by closed union types and are not the symbols named in this finding. Since Map.get only returns own entries, the described sink — a stored 'constructor'/'toString' resolving to an inherited Object.prototype member and surviving the ?? fallback — is not reachable at any of the four cited locations.
